name: Question 1
problem: Express the compound inequality $x<1$ or $x\ge \sqrt{2}$ using interval notation.
worked_solution:
We can represent the compound inequality on a number line, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191664/assets/e57c442c1524bf9c62feaefb1215cdfde23fee7dbbaf4207ce2e62bc8655769b.png)

The number line consists of the interval $(-\infty ,1)$ as well as the interval $[\sqrt{2},\infty ).$

So, we can express the compound inequality as the union of these two intervals:

$$
(-\infty ,1)\cup [\sqrt{2},\infty )
$$

Question 1
?

Express the compound inequality x<1 or x≥2 using interval notation.

a
(−∞,1]∪(2,∞)
b
(−∞,1)∪[2,∞)
c
(−∞,1)∪(2,∞)
d
(−∞,1]∪[2,∞)
e
(−∞,−2)∪[1,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can represent the compound inequality on a number line, as follows:

The number line consists of the interval (−∞,1) as well as the interval [2,∞).

So, we can express the compound inequality as the union of these two intervals: (−∞,1)∪[2,∞)
